div.head: ECf 32 A 10
div.ab: Non debent illa inuadiare nec extra regnum uendere, sed heredibus suis in extremis legare, ad seruitium tenementorum suorum dominis suis explendum, cum opus affuerit.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 656 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann prints some words here in smaller type (inuadiare, extra, uendere, heredibus); they are taken over from the Assize of Arms of 1181, which his margin names.
div.ab: They must not pledge them, nor sell them outside the kingdom, but bequeath them at their end to their heirs, for fulfilling the service of their tenements to their lords when need arises.
